issues.description: Close message type is wrong — PR description says 'CloseStream' but code sends 'Close'
issues.detail: The entire PR text and the linked Deepgram docs say the control message is {"type":"CloseStream"}. The code sends {"type":"Close"}. Either the PR description is a lie or the patch doesn't do what it claims. Both are unacceptable. Fix the string or fix the description, but the two have to match the actual API.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout is a guess, not a close handshake
issues.detail: You send Flush+Close then read exactly one frame and hope it's the ack. It could be a leftover audio frame, a binary chunk, or nothing. This is cargo-cult synchronization. Either drain until the server closes (with the timeout as an overall budget) or read until you see the specific ack message. One receive() with timeout is the wrong shape.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: Flush and Close are two different fixes bundled together
issues.detail: The commit message and title talk about CloseStream. The diff also unconditionally sends a Flush on every close. Flush-on-close is a behavior change with its own justification (or lack of one) and belongs in its own patch with its own reasoning. Don't smuggle behavior changes through a bugfix titled something else.

issues.description: Bare 'except Exception' swallows everything including CancelledError-adjacent bugs
issues.detail: Catching Exception around send_str/receive and logging a warning means a broken socket, a protocol error, and a logic bug all look identical in the logs. At minimum narrow to ConnectionError / aiohttp's WebSocketError. The STT path this claims to mirror should be the model; copy that handling, don't invent a new one.

issues.description: Class constants would be cleaner as module-level or shared with STT
issues.detail: _FLUSH_MSG and _CLOSE_MSG are constant JSON strings stuck on the class. The PR explicitly says STT already does this — so there's an existing constant somewhere. Reuse it instead of defining a parallel pair that will drift. Two copies of the same protocol string is exactly the bad-taste special-casing this review looks for.

issues.description: Commit message describes what, not why, and contradicts the diff
issues.detail: A future maintainer reading 'send CloseStream message' and then finding json.dumps({"type":"Close"}) will waste an hour. Commit messages exist so the maintainer-six-years-from-now doesn't curse you. Fix the message to match the wire protocol actually being sent, and explain why a 1s wait was chosen.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The headline bug is that the PR claims to send "CloseStream" while the code sends "Close" — one of them is wrong, and shipping a patch whose description doesn't match its diff is hostile to the next maintainer. The receive-once-with-timeout pattern is a guess at a handshake, not a handshake. Flush-on-close is a separate behavior change that got smuggled in; this should have been two patches. Bad taste in the bare except and the duplicated protocol constants that STT presumably already defines. Fix the wire string, reuse STT's constants, split the Flush change, and resubmit.
